titulo: The seven parts of a Jarvis
lead: Every agent, from the simplest to the most expensive, has the same seven parts: a door, a heart, an identity, a brain, a memory, hands, and a vault. Knowing these parts helps you choose better, spend less, and avoid getting locked into one product. INTELECTO is our example: small on purpose, so you can read through it.
objetivo: explain the path of a message and say what each of the seven parts does and where it lives in INTELECTO.

aprende.t: The path of a message, from Telegram to the model and back
What each of the seven pieces does
Why the loop with a brake sets an agent apart from a chatbot
How contracts let you swap one piece without changing the rest

hero_alt: Seven wooden blocks on a table, each with an object: phone, gear, card, chip, drawer, key, and padlock.

secoes.sub: Scroll the page: each step lights up a piece.

nos.detalhe: This is where you talk to it. In INTELECTO, that’s Telegram: one token and you’re ready, with no public internet address. The agent checks Telegram for new messages, splits replies longer than 4,000 characters, and shows “typing” while it thinks.

It receives your message, thinks, uses a tool if needed, checks the result, and thinks again until it replies with text. It has a brake: at most five tool rounds per message. After that, it has to reply.

Four simple files in the workspace folder: its soul, the rules, your profile, and the initial facts. The agent reads all four with every message. Change the text, change the assistant, without programming.
The AI model. In the cloud, OpenRouter: one key gives you access to more than a hundred models. On your computer, Ollama: no cost per message and nothing is sent outside your computer.
It saves what matters in a SQLite database on your machine, with keyword search and no API cost. With each message, it finds what’s relevant and adds it to the context.

Without tools, it only chats; with them, it gets things done. The core tools: read and write files, list folders, run commands, save to memory, and search memory. Each tool describes itself, and the model reads that description to decide whether to use it.
API keys encrypted and tied to the machine, a list of blocked commands, a 60-second timeout per command, and an audit log of everything it runs.

secoes.volta: The reply travels back through the channel to your phone
secoes.legenda: The same seven pieces appear in INTELECTO, OpenClaw, Hermes, or a Jarvis you build yourself.

rolagem_fim.texto: You write in Telegram. The loop brings together identity and memory, sends them to the model, runs the tool it requests within the vault’s limits, and sends the reply back through the same channel.

secoes.titulo: Three ideas that hold the pieces together

texto: INTELECTO is a personal assistant for one owner. It isn’t multiuser, doesn’t depend on the cloud, doesn’t need Docker, has no web dashboard, and isn’t a black box.
The plan calls for about three thousand lines and seven dependencies: you can read it.

exemplo.texto: Can I explain what happens between my message and the response? If not, it’s a black box.

texto: A chatbot responds and forgets. An agent thinks, acts with a tool, looks at the result, and thinks again.
Without a limit, an agent can keep spinning and spending without finishing. That’s why there’s a five-round brake.

exemplo.texto: At most 5 tool rounds per message; after that, respond with text.

texto: Each part is defined by a contract: the channel has start, send, and stop; the provider receives the conversation and tools, then returns a response.
Want WhatsApp instead of Telegram, or Ollama instead of OpenRouter? Use a different file with the same contract.

exemplo.texto: New tool = new file using the same pattern. The registry finds it automatically, without changing the core.

texto: The feature guide organizes everything into eight areas: identity, security, channels, memory, automation, integrations, skills, and architecture.
You don’t need everything. Scheduling and web search, for example, are in the plan for the next phase.

exemplo.texto: Loop + one brain + one channel + a basic SOUL. Memory comes right after.

secoes.sub: The core folder tree that the agent builds in the repository example.

blocos.conteudo:
jarvis/
  channels/    # the door: terminal and Telegram
  agent/       # the heart: loop.py and context.py
  providers/   # the brain: contract + test model
  memory/      # the memory: SQLite with search
  tools/       # the hands: files, command, memory
  security/    # the vault: secrets and blocklist
workspace/
  SOUL.md  AGENTS.md  USER.md  MEMORY.md   # the identity

abas.html:
1. You write in Telegram.
  2. The channel receives it and passes it to the loop.
  3. The loop builds the context: SOUL + AGENTS + USER and relevant memories.
  4. The model responds or requests a tool; the loop runs it and returns the result (up to 5 rounds).
  5. The response goes back through the channel.

Chatbot: responds, forgets when the conversation ends, has no identity, doesn’t act, and doesn’t know you.

Jarvis: remembers past conversations, has a name and written values, uses tools, and knows your context.

secoes.sub: Before you build, understand what you’re going to build.

The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: What makes an agent more than just a chatbot?
opcoes: The loop: think, use a tool, check the result, and think again until it can answer.
perguntas.explica: The loop turns conversation into action. The model can stay the same; what changes is its ability to use tools and check the result before answering.

perguntas.p: What is the five-tool-round limit for?
opcoes: It’s a brake: without it, the agent can keep going in circles and spending money without ever finishing.
To make the model think less.
perguntas.explica: The cap makes the agent answer after five rounds. A short, clear loop with a limit is what separates a useful agent from one that spends endlessly.

perguntas.p: You want to switch from Telegram to WhatsApp. What changes?
opcoes: You have to rewrite the whole agent.
A new channel file that follows the same contract (start, send, stop); everything else stays the same.
You also have to switch models.
You can’t: INTELECTO only works with Telegram.
perguntas.explica: Each part has a contract. A new channel implements the same three functions, and the loop doesn’t even notice the switch.

perguntas.p: Where does the assistant’s personality live?
opcoes: In four text files in the workspace folder.
perguntas.explica: SOUL, AGENTS, USER, and MEMORY are plain text. The agent reads all four with every message: change the text, and you change the assistant.
